# The Rental Market {#sec-market-rental}

<!-- Purpose: rental-market dynamics — who rents, what they pay, the professional apartment market, FMRs, and the assisted-inventory preservation picture (PLAN.md §7 Ch 3b).
     Narrative: prose migrated from the team Google Doc draft (Oct 2026); numbers audited against the data. -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("_common.R")

stock <- read_rds("data/acs_stock.rds")
costs <- read_rds("data/acs_costs.rds")
costar <- read_rds("data/costar.rds")
fmr   <- read_rds("data/fmr.rds")
nhpd  <- read_rds("data/nhpd.rds")
fred  <- read_rds("data/fred.rds")
mls   <- read_rds("data/mls.rds")

# Palette anchors (match ggtext subtitle spans to line/fill colors)
blue   <- hda_pal[1]
green  <- hda_pal[2]
yellow <- hda_pal[3]
coral  <- hda_pal[4]

# CPI deflator to the latest full year (2026 CPI is still NA) — real dollars = base-year dollars
cpi_base_year <- max(fred$cpi$year[!is.na(fred$cpi$cpi_less_shelter)])   # 2025
cpi_base      <- fred$cpi$cpi_less_shelter[fred$cpi$year == cpi_base_year]

geo_label <- function(GEOID, geo_type) case_when(
  GEOID == fauquier  ~ "Fauquier County",
  GEOID == "5183136" ~ "Warrenton",
  GEOID == "5105336" ~ "Bealeton",
  geo_type == "state" ~ "Virginia"
)

# Collapse B25032 renter-side (units 013–023) to 6 structure types — mirrors inventory's B25024
structure_cat32 <- function(v) case_when(
  v == "B25032_014"                   ~ "Single-family detached",
  v == "B25032_015"                   ~ "Single-family attached",
  v %in% c("B25032_016", "B25032_017") ~ "2–4 units",
  v %in% c("B25032_018", "B25032_019") ~ "5–19 units",
  v %in% c("B25032_020", "B25032_021") ~ "20+ units",
  v %in% c("B25032_022", "B25032_023") ~ "Mobile home / other"
)
struct_lvls <- c("Single-family detached", "Single-family attached", "2–4 units",
                 "5–19 units", "20+ units", "Mobile home / other")

# --- Inline scalars for bullet text -----------------------------------------
b3 <- stock$b25003_trend |> filter(year == 2024)
rshare <- \(g) {
  d <- b3[b3$GEOID == g, ]
  d$estimate[str_ends(d$variable, "003")] / d$estimate[str_ends(d$variable, "001")]
}
rshare_county <- rshare(fauquier)         # 0.212
rshare_warr   <- rshare("5183136")        # 0.370
rshare_beal   <- rshare("5105336")        # 0.213
rshare_va     <- rshare(virginia)         # 0.327

# County gross rent, nominal + real (B25064 trend)
rent_c <- costs$trend_rent |> filter(GEOID == fauquier) |> select(year, rent = estimate)
rent_13 <- rent_c$rent[rent_c$year == 2013]
rent_24 <- rent_c$rent[rent_c$year == 2024]
cpi13   <- fred$cpi$cpi_less_shelter[fred$cpi$year == 2013]
rent_growth_nom  <- rent_24 / rent_13 - 1
cpi24            <- fred$cpi$cpi_less_shelter[fred$cpi$year == 2024]
prices_growth_13_24 <- cpi24 / cpi13 - 1          # everyday prices (CPI less shelter), 2013–2024

# CoStar professional market — nominal, split Market vs Affordable (rent_type from the property file)
cs_q      <- costar$quarterly
cs_t      <- costar$quarterly_type
cs_latest <- cs_q |> slice_max(year * 10 + qtr, n = 1)
cs_units  <- cs_latest$market_units
cs_props  <- cs_latest$n_properties
cs_vac_recent <- mean(tail(cs_q$vacancy_rate, 4))   # last 4 quarters
cs_vac_latest <- cs_latest$vacancy_rate
cs_vac_early  <- mean(cs_q$vacancy_rate[cs_q$year %in% 2019:2021])
cs_vac_share_u3 <- mean(cs_q$vacancy_rate < 3, na.rm = TRUE)    # share of quarters under 3%
cs_props_total <- nrow(costar$properties)         # properties in the broader CoStar inventory
cs_tl  <- cs_t |> slice_max(year * 10 + qtr, n = 1, by = rent_type)
cs_tv  <- \(type, col) cs_tl[[col]][cs_tl$rent_type == type]
cs_t16 <- \(type) cs_t$asking_rent_avg[cs_t$rent_type == type & cs_t$year == 2016 & cs_t$qtr == 1]
cs_growth <- \(type) cs_tv(type, "asking_rent_avg") / cs_t16(type) - 1
cpi16 <- fred$cpi$cpi_less_shelter[fred$cpi$year == 2016]
prices_growth_16_25 <- cpi_base / cpi16 - 1
cs_vac_prev_yr <- \(type) cs_t$vacancy_rate[cs_t$rent_type == type & cs_t$year == cs_latest$year - 1 &
                                              cs_t$qtr == cs_latest$qtr]

# Property-level detail behind the latest vacancy reading
cs_latest_prop <- costar$quarterly_prop |>
  filter(year == cs_latest$year, qtr == cs_latest$qtr, !is.na(asking_rent), units > 0)
cs_top_vac <- cs_latest_prop |> slice_max(vacancy * units, n = 1)
cs_conc    <- costar$properties |> filter(property_address == cs_top_vac$address) |> pull(avg_concessions_percent)

# Pipeline
cs_pipe <- costar$properties |> filter(building_status != "Existing")

# MLS closed leases by year (same lease-price screen as r/gaps.R)
lease_yr <- mls$rentals |>
  filter(between(lease_price, 200, 15000)) |>
  summarize(median = median(lease_price), n = n(), u1700 = mean(lease_price < 1700), .by = year) |>
  arrange(year)
ly <- \(y, col) lease_yr[[col]][lease_yr$year == y]

# Rental stock by structure (renter side)
r_struct <- stock$b25032 |>
  filter(geo_type == "county", as.integer(str_sub(variable, -3)) >= 14) |>
  mutate(cat = structure_cat32(variable)) |>
  summarize(est = sum(estimate), .by = cat) |>
  mutate(share = est / sum(est))
sf_share  <- sum(r_struct$share[r_struct$cat %in% c("Single-family detached", "Single-family attached")])
apt_share <- sum(r_struct$share[r_struct$cat %in% c("5–19 units", "20+ units")])

# FMR vs actual (2BR)
fmr_2br <- fmr$fmr$fmr_2br
acs_2br <- costs$B25031$estimate[costs$B25031$GEOID == fauquier & costs$B25031$variable == "B25031_004"]

# NHPD assisted inventory
nhpd_props   <- nrow(nhpd$properties)
nhpd_assist  <- sum(nhpd$properties$total_assisted_units, na.rm = TRUE)
nhpd_soonest <- min(nhpd$properties$earliest_expiration, na.rm = TRUE)
nhpd_10yr    <- sum(nhpd$properties$earliest_expiration <= as.Date("2036-12-31"), na.rm = TRUE)
nhpd_city    <- nhpd$properties |> summarize(props = n(), units = sum(total_units), .by = city)
nc <- \(c, col) nhpd_city[[col]][nhpd_city$city == c]

# MLS rentals (2025) — interview validation anchors
r25 <- mls$rentals |> filter(year == 2025)
rent_n_2025   <- nrow(r25)
rent_u1700    <- sum(r25$lease_price < 1700, na.rm = TRUE)
rent_median   <- median(r25$lease_price, na.rm = TRUE)

# MLS rentals, 2026 year to date (closed leases) and the current active rental snapshot
r26 <- mls$rentals |> filter(year == 2026)
rent_n_2026   <- nrow(r26)
rent_med_2026 <- median(r26$lease_price, na.rm = TRUE)
rent_thru     <- format(max(r26$lease_date, na.rm = TRUE), "%B %Y")
ar <- mls$active_rentals |> filter(!is.na(list_price), list_price > 0)
ar_n      <- nrow(ar)
ar_med    <- median(ar$list_price)
ar_u1700  <- sum(ar$list_price < 1700)
ar_asof   <- format(max(mls$active_rentals$snapshot_date), "%B %Y")
```

## Who rents

```{r}
#| label: fig-renter-share
#| fig-cap: "Warrenton is the county's clearest concentration of renters"
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of the renter share of occupied households in 2024 for Warrenton, Fauquier County, Bealeton, and Virginia. Warrenton is about 37% renter, well above Fauquier County and Bealeton at roughly 21% each; Virginia sits at about 33%. Renter household counts are labeled on each bar."

f1 <- b3 |>
  summarize(
    total  = estimate[str_ends(variable, "001")],
    renter = estimate[str_ends(variable, "003")],
    moe    = moe[str_ends(variable, "003")],
    cv     = cv[str_ends(variable, "003")],
    .by = c(GEOID, geo_type)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    share = renter / total,
    geo = geo_label(GEOID, geo_type)
  ) |>
  flag_reliability() |>
  # Bealeton floor: suppress Low cells (none here); footnote Medium
  mutate(
    share = if_else(reliability == "Low", NA_real_, share),
    geo = fct_reorder(geo, share)
  )

ggplot(f1, aes(share, geo)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = geo == "Warrenton"), width = 0.68) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(label_percent(accuracy = 1)(share),
                               "  (", format(round(renter), big.mark = ","), " HH",
                               if_else(reliability == "Medium", "*", ""), ")")),
            hjust = -0.05, size = 3.2, color = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = coral, `FALSE` = blue), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(c(0, 0.22)), limits = c(0, 0.45)) +
  labs(
    title = "Warrenton is the county's clearest concentration of renters",
    subtitle = "Renter share of occupied households, 2024 (renter-household counts labeled)",
    caption = paste0(acs_cap("B25003"),
                     " *Bealeton renter count is Medium reliability (CV 15–30%)."),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hda(flip_gridlines = TRUE) +
  add_zero_line("x")
```

Fauquier is overwhelmingly an ownership county: only about `r label_percent(accuracy = 1)(rshare_county)` of households rent. For context, `r label_percent(accuracy = 1)(rshare_va)` of Virginia's households are renters. Folks come to Fauquier to buy, and there is a limited rental market.

Warrenton is the exception: roughly `r label_percent(accuracy = 1)(rshare_warr)` of the town's `r format(round(b3$estimate[b3$GEOID=="5183136" & str_ends(b3$variable,"001")]), big.mark=",")` households rent, nearly double the county rate. Warrenton represents the county's principal rental submarket. Bealeton, on the other hand, tracks with the county at about `r label_percent(accuracy = 1)(rshare_beal)` of its households renting.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Reliability
Bealeton's renter count is small and carries Medium reliability, so it is read as a count, not a precise rate.
:::

## What renters pay

```{r}
#| label: fig-rent-trend
#| fig-cap: "Every measure of rent has climbed, and broker-placed leases run highest"
#| fig-alt: !expr 'paste0("Line chart of Fauquier County rents in current dollars. The ACS median gross rent rises from about ", label_dollar()(rent_13), " in 2013 to ", label_dollar()(rent_24), " in 2024. CoStar asking rents, quarterly from 2016, climb at market-rate apartments to about ", label_dollar()(round(cs_tv("Market", "asking_rent_avg"))), " and at affordable (rent-restricted or subsidized) apartments to about ", label_dollar()(round(cs_tv("Affordable", "asking_rent_avg"))), ". The MLS median closed lease, mostly single-family homes and townhouses, runs highest, rising from ", label_dollar()(ly(2022, "median")), " in 2022 to ", label_dollar()(ly(max(lease_yr$year), "median")), " in 2026 to date. Town points for Warrenton and Bealeton sit near the county ACS line.")'

county_rent <- costs$trend_rent |>
  filter(GEOID == fauquier) |>
  transmute(date = make_date(year, 7L, 1L), rent = estimate, series = "ACS median gross rent")

town_rent <- costs$trend_rent |>
  filter(geo_type == "place") |>
  flag_reliability() |>
  mutate(rent = if_else(reliability == "Low", NA_real_, estimate),
         town = geo_label(GEOID, geo_type),
         date = make_date(year, 7L, 1L))

costar_rent <- cs_t |>
  transmute(date = make_date(year, (qtr - 1) * 3 + 1, 1L), rent = asking_rent_avg,
            series = paste0("CoStar ", str_to_lower(rent_type), " apartments"))

mls_rent <- lease_yr |>
  transmute(date = make_date(year, 7L, 1L), rent = median, series = "MLS closed leases")

rent_cols <- c("ACS median gross rent" = blue, "CoStar market apartments" = green,
               "CoStar affordable apartments" = yellow, "MLS closed leases" = coral)

ggplot(mapping = aes(date, rent, color = series)) +
  geom_line(data = county_rent, linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_line(data = costar_rent, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_line(data = mls_rent, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = mls_rent, size = 1.8) +
  geom_point(data = town_rent, aes(group = town), color = "grey45", size = 1.4) +
  geom_text(data = filter(town_rent, year == 2024), aes(label = town),
            color = "grey40", hjust = 0, nudge_x = 60, size = 2.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = rent_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(), expand = expansion(c(0.03, 0.06))) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y",
               expand = expansion(c(0.02, 0.14))) +
  labs(
    title = "Every measure of rent has climbed, and broker-placed leases run highest",
    subtitle = "Monthly rent, current dollars — <span style='color:#445ca9'>**ACS median gross rent**</span> (grey points = towns)<br>CoStar asking rent at <span style='color:#8baeaa'>**market-rate**</span> and <span style='color:#e9ab3f'>**affordable**</span> apartments; <span style='color:#e76f52'>**MLS closed-lease median**</span>",
    caption = paste0(acs_cap("B25064"), "<br>", costar_cap(), "<br>", mls_cap("2022–2026, 2026 year to date")),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hda() +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_markdown())
```

The county's median gross rent, meaning all housing costs including lease rent and utilities, rose from $`r format(rent_13, big.mark=",")` in 2013 to $`r format(rent_24, big.mark=",")` in 2024, an increase of `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(rent_growth_nom)`. Over the same years, prices for everyday goods and services other than housing rose about `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(prices_growth_13_24)`, so rents have outpaced general inflation and renters have lost ground.

The other rent measures tell the same story at different price points. CoStar asking rents at the county's market-rate apartments reached about $`r format(round(cs_tv("Market", "asking_rent_avg")), big.mark=",")` in `r costar_through`, `r if (cs_tv("Market", "asking_rent_avg") > rent_24) "above" else "below"` the ACS median, while the larger set of affordable (rent-restricted or subsidized) apartments asked about $`r format(round(cs_tv("Affordable", "asking_rent_avg")), big.mark=",")`. The MLS median closed lease kept rising after the ACS series ends, from $`r format(ly(2022, "median"), big.mark=",")` in 2022 to $`r format(ly(max(lease_yr$year), "median"), big.mark=",")` in 2026 to date; these broker-placed leases skew toward single-family homes and townhouses and price well above the other measures. This report uses the ACS median gross rent as its affordability benchmark (@sec-gaps), since it covers the full rental universe, while CoStar tracks only professionally managed apartment communities.

::: {.callout-note title="What we heard"}
In spring 2026, an interviewee shared that "Only about 2 of 19 available rentals were priced under $1,700."
:::

Town rents track the county: Warrenton and Bealeton median 2024 rent (High reliability) sits roughly within $50 to $200 of the county figure.

## Where the rental stock prices

```{r}
#| label: fig-rent-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Most rentals now price at $1,500 or more"
#| fig-alt: "Grouped bar chart of the gross rent distribution for cash-rent renters in Fauquier County, Warrenton, and Bealeton across six rent bands. The $1,500–$1,999 band is the largest in the county at roughly a quarter of renters, and shares rise sharply above $1,000; bands under $1,000 are thin. Town bars with too few sample cases are omitted."

band_lvls <- c("<$1,000", "$1,000–1,249", "$1,250–1,499", "$1,500–1,999",
               "$2,000–2,499", "$2,500+")
band_of <- function(v) {
  n <- as.integer(str_sub(v, -3))
  case_when(
    n %in% 3:19 ~ "<$1,000",
    n == 20     ~ "$1,000–1,249",
    n == 21     ~ "$1,250–1,499",
    n == 22     ~ "$1,500–1,999",
    n == 23     ~ "$2,000–2,499",
    n %in% 24:26 ~ "$2,500+"
  )
}

rd <- costs$B25063 |>
  filter(geo_type %in% c("county", "place")) |>
  mutate(band = band_of(variable)) |>
  filter(!is.na(band)) |>
  summarize(est = sum(estimate), moe = sqrt(sum(moe^2)), .by = c(GEOID, geo_type, band)) |>
  mutate(
    share = est / sum(est),
    cv = if_else(est > 0, (moe / 1.645) / est * 100, NA_real_),
    .by = GEOID
  ) |>
  flag_reliability() |>
  mutate(
    share = if_else(reliability == "Low" | is.na(reliability), NA_real_, share),  # Bealeton floor
    band = factor(band, levels = band_lvls),
    geo = factor(geo_label(GEOID, geo_type),
                 levels = c("Fauquier County", "Warrenton", "Bealeton"))
  )

ggplot(rd, aes(band, share, fill = geo)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(preserve = "single"), width = 0.72) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1), expand = expansion(c(0, 0.05))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`Fauquier County` = blue, Warrenton = green, Bealeton = yellow)) +
  labs(
    title = "Most rentals now price at $1,500 or more",
    subtitle = "Distribution of gross rent among cash-rent renters, 2024",
    caption = paste0(acs_cap("B25063"),
                     " Town bands with a coefficient of variation above 30% are omitted (small samples)."),
    x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hda() +
  add_zero_line("y") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8))
```

The modal rent band in the county is $1,500–1,999 and represents about `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(rd$share[rd$GEOID==fauquier & rd$band=="$1,500–1,999"])` of county cash-rent renters. Combined with the bands above it, most renters now pay $1,500 or more. Under $1,000 monthly rentals are scarce, representing only about `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(rd$share[rd$GEOID==fauquier & rd$band=="<$1,000"])` of the county's renters, underscoring how little of the stock is affordable to lower-income households.

::: {.callout-note title="What we heard"}
Realtors in particular recognized the challenges renters face, noting that the MLS median rent sits at $2,450: "It's an outrageously expensive market." Rental quality was a consistent topic as well, with interviewees reporting that quality is rarely reflected in the price.
:::

In 2025, the MLS recorded that only `r rent_u1700` of `r rent_n_2025` closed leases were under $1,700, about `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(rent_u1700/rent_n_2025)`. That share has shrunk quickly, from `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(ly(2022, "u1700"))` of leases in 2022 to `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(ly(max(lease_yr$year), "u1700"))` in 2026 to date. These data identify a median county lease of $`r format(rent_median, big.mark=",")` monthly, consistent with the Greater Piedmont REALTOR's March 2026 study. This leaves a somewhat larger affordable share than the single snapshot of available rentals suggested, but the story is the same: sub-$1,700 rentals are scarce, and most of the rental market prices well above that (@fig-rent-distribution, @fig-rent-trend). The MLS median runs well above the county's ACS median gross rent ($`r format(rent_24, big.mark=",")`) because MLS only captures leases placed through a broker, which skew toward larger single-family homes and townhouses (the bulk of this study's rental stock) rather than the smaller apartment units that lease in-house and never reach MLS.

::: {.callout-note}
## What is listed for rent now
As of `r ar_asof`, the MLS shows **`r ar_n` active rental listings** with a median asking rent of **$`r format(ar_med, big.mark=",")`**, well above the 2025 closed-lease median of $`r format(rent_median, big.mark=",")` and the $`r format(rent_med_2026, big.mark=",")` median across `r rent_n_2026` leases closed so far in 2026 (through `r rent_thru`). Only `r ar_u1700` listings (`r label_percent(accuracy=0.1)(ar_u1700/ar_n)`) ask under $1,700, fewer in share than the 2025 closed leases (`r label_percent(accuracy=1)(rent_u1700/rent_n_2025)`). Asking rents run above closed leases and this is a small single-day snapshot, so read it as directional rather than as a market-wide rent.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## Data note: place-level distributions
Place-level distributions are noisy; only the higher-count Warrenton bands survive the reliability screen, and they mirror the county's upward concentration.
:::

## The professional apartment market

```{r}
#| label: fig-costar
#| fig-cap: "Apartment rents keep rising at market-rate and affordable properties"
#| fig-alt: !expr 'paste0("Line chart of quarterly CoStar asking rent per unit in current dollars, Fauquier County, 2016 through ", costar_through, ", split by property type. Market-rate apartments rise from about ", label_dollar()(round(cs_t16("Market"))), " to about ", label_dollar()(round(cs_tv("Market", "asking_rent_avg"))), "; affordable (rent-restricted or subsidized) apartments rise from about ", label_dollar()(round(cs_t16("Affordable"))), " to about ", label_dollar()(round(cs_tv("Affordable", "asking_rent_avg"))), ", dipping slightly in the latest quarter.")'

cs_rent <- cs_t |>
  mutate(date = make_date(year, (qtr - 1) * 3 + 1, 1L),
         rent_type = factor(rent_type, levels = c("Market", "Affordable")))

ggplot(cs_rent, aes(date, asking_rent_avg, color = rent_type)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = slice_max(cs_rent, date, by = rent_type),
            aes(label = paste0(rent_type, "\n", label_dollar()(round(asking_rent_avg)))),
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3, fontface = "bold", lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Market = green, Affordable = yellow), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(), limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y", expand = expansion(c(0.02, 0.14))) +
  labs(
    title = "Apartment rents keep rising at market-rate and affordable properties",
    subtitle = paste0("Average monthly asking rent per unit, current dollars<br><span style='color:#8baeaa'>**Market-rate**</span> (",
                      cs_tv("Market", "total_units"), " units) and <span style='color:#e9ab3f'>**affordable**</span> (",
                      cs_tv("Affordable", "total_units"), " units) CoStar-tracked properties"),
    caption = paste0(costar_cap(), "<br>Affordable = rent-restricted, subsidized or mixed-income properties per CoStar."),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hda() +
  add_zero_line("y") +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_markdown())
```

The professional rental market is small. Roughly `r cs_props_total` multifamily properties appear in the broader CoStar inventory, and CoStar tracks quarterly rents at `r cs_props` apartment properties with about `r label_comma()(cs_units)` units. Most of those units, about `r label_comma()(cs_tv("Affordable", "total_units"))`, are at affordable properties that are rent-restricted or subsidized; only about `r cs_tv("Market", "total_units")` are at market-rate properties.

Asking rents at the market-rate properties averaged about $`r format(round(cs_tv("Market", "asking_rent_avg")), big.mark=",")` in `r costar_through`, up `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(cs_growth("Market"))` since early 2016. Affordable properties asked about $`r format(round(cs_tv("Affordable", "asking_rent_avg")), big.mark=",")`, up `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(cs_growth("Affordable"))`. For comparison, prices for everyday goods and services other than housing rose about `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(prices_growth_16_25)` from 2016 to 2025, so apartment rents of both kinds have outpaced general inflation.

`r if (nrow(cs_pipe) > 0) paste0("New supply is on the way. ", cs_pipe$property_name[1], ", a ", cs_pipe$number_of_units[1], "-unit market-rate community in ", cs_pipe$city[1], ", is ", str_to_lower(cs_pipe$building_status[1]), " with asking rents near $", label_comma()(cs_pipe$avg_asking_unit[1]), ". That would nearly double the market-rate apartment units CoStar tracks, at rents well above the current market-rate average (@sec-inventory).") else ""`

```{r}
#| label: fig-costar-vacancy
#| fig-cap: "Apartment vacancy has edged up, driven by affordable properties"
#| fig-alt: !expr 'paste0("Line chart of quarterly CoStar vacancy rates, Fauquier County, 2016 through ", costar_through, ". The overall rate falls from about 5% to near 1% around 2019–2021, then rises to about ", label_percent(accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1)(cs_vac_latest), " in the latest quarter. Affordable properties drive the increase, reaching about ", label_percent(accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1)(cs_tv("Affordable", "vacancy_rate")), ", while market-rate properties stay near ", label_percent(accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1)(cs_tv("Market", "vacancy_rate")), ".")'

cs_vac <- bind_rows(
  cs_q |> transmute(year, qtr, series = "All tracked", vacancy_rate),
  cs_t |> transmute(year, qtr, series = rent_type, vacancy_rate)
) |>
  filter(!is.na(vacancy_rate)) |>
  mutate(date = make_date(year, (qtr - 1) * 3 + 1, 1L),
         series = factor(series, levels = c("All tracked", "Market", "Affordable")))

ggplot(cs_vac, aes(date, vacancy_rate, color = series, linewidth = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_text(data = slice_max(cs_vac, date, by = series),
            aes(label = series), hjust = -0.1, size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`All tracked` = coral, Market = green, Affordable = yellow), guide = "none") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(`All tracked` = 1.2, Market = 0.7, Affordable = 0.7), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1, accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, NA),
                     breaks = seq(0, 12, 2), expand = expansion(c(0, 0.08))) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y", expand = expansion(c(0.02, 0.14))) +
  labs(
    title = "Apartment vacancy has edged up, driven by affordable properties",
    subtitle = "Unit-weighted vacancy rate, CoStar-tracked apartments<br><span style='color:#e76f52'>**All tracked**</span>, <span style='color:#8baeaa'>**market-rate**</span>, and <span style='color:#e9ab3f'>**affordable**</span> properties",
    caption = costar_cap(), x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hda() +
  add_zero_line("y") +
  theme(plot.subtitle = element_markdown())
```

Fauquier's professional rental market remains tight, though slack has crept in. Vacancy across the tracked apartments averaged about `r label_percent(accuracy=0.1, scale=1)(cs_vac_recent)` over the last four quarters (`r label_percent(accuracy=0.1, scale=1)(cs_vac_latest)` in `r costar_through`), up from about `r label_percent(accuracy=0.1, scale=1)(cs_vac_early)` in 2019–2021. Even so, it has been under 3% in `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(cs_vac_share_u3)` of quarters since 2016. The increase sits at the affordable properties, where vacancy reached about `r label_percent(accuracy=0.1, scale=1)(cs_tv("Affordable", "vacancy_rate"))` (`r label_percent(accuracy=0.1, scale=1)(cs_vac_prev_yr("Affordable"))` a year earlier); market-rate vacancy is about `r label_percent(accuracy=0.1, scale=1)(cs_tv("Market", "vacancy_rate"))`. Much of it comes from one property: `r cs_top_vac$building` (`r cs_top_vac$units` units) reports `r cs_top_vac$vacancy`% vacancy and `r round(cs_conc, 1)`% concessions in the latest quarter.

## Rental stock by structure type

```{r}
#| label: fig-rental-structure
#| fig-cap: "Most of Fauquier's rental stock is single-family homes, not apartments"
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of Fauquier County's renter-occupied housing units by structure type. Single-family detached homes are the largest share at about 57% of rentals, followed by 20-plus-unit buildings and 5-to-19-unit buildings; single-family detached and attached together make up roughly two-thirds of the rental stock."

rs <- r_struct |>
  mutate(cat = factor(cat, levels = rev(struct_lvls)))

ggplot(rs, aes(share, cat)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = str_starts(as.character(cat), "Single-family")), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label_percent(accuracy = 1)(share)),
            hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2, color = "grey20") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = blue, `FALSE` = green), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Most of Fauquier's rental stock is single-family homes, not apartments",
    subtitle = "Share of renter-occupied units by structure type, Fauquier County, 2020–2024",
    caption = acs_cap("B25032"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hda(flip_gridlines = TRUE) +
  add_zero_line("x")
```

Single-family homes are the backbone of the county's rental market, about `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(sf_share)` of all renter-occupied units (attached and detached). Single-family detached alone is roughly `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(r_struct$share[r_struct$cat=="Single-family detached"])` of the rental market.

Purpose-built apartments (5+ units) are only about `r label_percent(accuracy=1)(apt_share)` of rentals, the mirror image of @fig-costar's thin professional market. This could be why so much of the rental supply behaves like the for-sale market: the reliance on scattered single-family rentals means renters compete for the same limited housing stock as buyers.[^rental-structure]

[^rental-structure]: Place-level structure detail is too small to size reliably, so this is shown county-wide.

## Fair Market Rents vs. actual rents

```{r}
#| label: fig-fmr
#| fig-cap: "Metro Fair Market Rents run well above what Fauquier renters actually pay"
#| fig-alt: "Dot-and-range chart comparing rents by bedroom size in Fauquier County. For one- through four-bedroom units, the HUD metro-area Fair Market Rent sits far above the ACS actual median gross rent; the Small Area FMR range across the three town ZIP codes falls between the two but still above the local median. The gap is largest for one- and two-bedroom units."

br_map <- tibble(
  bedrooms = factor(c("1BR", "2BR", "3BR", "4BR"), levels = c("1BR", "2BR", "3BR", "4BR")),
  acs_var  = c("B25031_003", "B25031_004", "B25031_005", "B25031_006"),
  fmr      = c(fmr$fmr$fmr_1br, fmr$fmr$fmr_2br, fmr$fmr$fmr_3br, fmr$fmr$fmr_4br)
)

acs_actual <- costs$B25031 |>
  filter(GEOID == fauquier) |>
  select(acs_var = variable, acs = estimate)

safmr_rng <- fmr$safmr |>
  summarize(across(c(safmr_1br, safmr_2br, safmr_3br, safmr_4br), list(lo = min, hi = max))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("br", ".value"), names_pattern = "safmr_(\\d)br_(lo|hi)") |>
  transmute(bedrooms = factor(paste0(br, "BR"), levels = c("1BR", "2BR", "3BR", "4BR")), lo, hi)

f6 <- br_map |>
  left_join(acs_actual, by = "acs_var") |>
  left_join(safmr_rng, by = "bedrooms")

ggplot(f6, aes(bedrooms)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), color = green, linewidth = 6, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_point(aes(y = fmr, color = "Metro FMR"), size = 3.4) +
  geom_point(aes(y = acs, color = "ACS actual median"), size = 3.4) +
  geom_text(aes(y = fmr, label = label_dollar()(fmr)), vjust = -1, size = 2.8, color = coral) +
  geom_text(aes(y = acs, label = label_dollar()(acs)), vjust = 1.9, size = 2.8, color = blue) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Metro FMR" = coral, "ACS actual median" = blue), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(), expand = expansion(c(0.05, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Metro Fair Market Rents run well above what Fauquier renters actually pay",
    subtitle = "By bedroom size — <span style='color:#e76f52'>**HUD metro FMR**</span>, <span style='color:#445ca9'>**ACS actual median rent**</span>, and the <span style='color:#8baeaa'>**Small Area FMR range**</span> across town ZIPs, FY2026",
    caption = paste0(fmr_cap(), " ", acs_cap("B25031")),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_hda() +
  add_zero_line("y") +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.subtitle = element_markdown())
```

Because Fauquier is folded into the high-cost Washington, D.C. metro FMR area, the county's two bedroom (2BR) FMR at $`r format(fmr_2br, big.mark=",")` sits far above the actual ACS median 2BR rent of $`r format(acs_2br, big.mark=",")`. This is a gap of roughly $`r format(round((fmr_2br-acs_2br)/50)*50, big.mark=",")`.

Small Area FMRs (SAFMRs) pull the benchmark towards what locals actually experience, described as a high cost and scarce rental environment. SAFMRs still land above the ACS median rent at every bedroom size, with the Warrenton and Bealeton 2BR SAFMR ranges from $`r format(min(fmr$safmr$safmr_2br), big.mark=",")` to $`r format(max(fmr$safmr$safmr_2br), big.mark=",")`, with Bealeton (22712) at the lowest.

The practical implication in the differences in FMR and ACS rents is ultimately favorable for voucher holders, with generous payment standards. However, this means FMRs overstate the going asking rental market and can be a poor gauge of local affordability. The ACS medians (@fig-rent-trend) are the better yardstick for rooting rents into local reality.

::: {.callout-note title="What we heard"}
An interviewee noted that metro-based Fair Market Rents give voucher holders generous payment standards relative to what local rents actually are.
:::

## Assisted inventory & preservation risk

```{r}
#| label: tbl-nhpd
#| tbl-cap: "Federally assisted rental properties, sorted by earliest subsidy expiration"
#| fig-alt: "Table of the county's 13 federally assisted rental properties with their town, total and assisted unit counts, subsidy programs, and earliest subsidy expiration. The 874 assisted units are concentrated in and around Warrenton and dominated by Low-Income Housing Tax Credit deals; expirations begin in January 2027 and 8 of the 13 properties have a subsidy lapsing by 2036."

prog_by_prop <- nhpd$programs |>
  distinct(nhpd_id, program_name) |>
  filter(!is.na(program_name)) |>
  summarize(programs = paste(sort(unique(program_name)), collapse = ", "), .by = nhpd_id)

nhpd_tbl <- nhpd$properties |>
  left_join(prog_by_prop, by = "nhpd_id") |>
  arrange(earliest_expiration) |>
  transmute(
    Property = str_to_title(property_name),
    City = city,
    Units = total_units,
    `Assisted units` = total_assisted_units,
    Programs = coalesce(programs, "—"),
    `Earliest expiration` = format(earliest_expiration, "%b %Y")
  )

nhpd_tbl |>
  kbl(align = "llrrll") |>
  kable_styling(c("condensed", "striped"), full_width = FALSE) |>
  footnote(
    general = tbl_note(paste0(nhpd_cap(),
                     " Assisted-unit counts may exceed total units where a property carries overlapping subsidies. ",
                     "Programs list active subsidy types per property.")),
    general_title = "", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE, escape = FALSE
  )
```

Fauquier's assisted housing rental stock consists of `r format(nhpd_assist, big.mark=",")` units across `r nhpd_props` federally supported properties. This is a small cushion against the market rents documented above. The program mix locally is dominated by Low-Income Housing Tax Credit deals, with a handful of older project-based Section 8, PRAC/811 (elderly/disabled project rental assistance), and USDA Rural Housing (515) properties whose subsidies are the closest to expiring.

Rental affordability preservation at these properties is a real risk and near-term, with the soonest subsidy expiration in `r format(nhpd_soonest, "%B %Y")`. Additionally, `r nhpd_10yr` of the `r nhpd_props` properties have a subsidy expiring by 2036, the window in which preservation decisions must be made. As assistance units are aging, the quality of these rentals throughout the county is likely lower comparatively to the other aging single family rentals.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Town spotlight — assisted units concentrate in and around Warrenton
**Most of the county's assisted properties sit in Warrenton** (`r nc("Warrenton", "props")` of `r nhpd_props`, about `r nc("Warrenton", "units")` units), the same submarket that carries the county's highest renter share (@fig-renter-share). **Bealeton has a smaller assisted base** of `r nc("Bealeton", "props")` properties and about `r nc("Bealeton", "units")` units, including the Mintbrook senior apartments. Beyond those, affordable options in Bealeton depend on scattered single-family and market-rate units that price low, which @fig-rent-distribution **shows is a shrinking share**.`r if (nrow(cs_pipe) > 0 && cs_pipe$city[1] == "Bealeton") paste0(" The ", cs_pipe$number_of_units[1], "-unit ", cs_pipe$property_name[1], " will add market-rate apartments to the town, asking about $", label_comma()(cs_pipe$avg_asking_unit[1]), " a month.")`
:::
